blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision transformers are strong but costly image encoders for video object segmentation. Training-free token merging cuts compute uniformly across the frame, including on tracked objects. We give a frozen DINOv3 ViT inside a trained Cutie head a training-free focus map: full resolution where the segmenter expects its objects and coarser merging elsewhere. Protecting only the previous frame's mask works on short clips but fails on long videos, where fast motion pushes targets outside the margin and into background merging, locking in loss. Our policy instead takes the union of velocity-shifted and block-matched masks, runs a camera-compensated surprise check, delegates uncertain regions to the compared merger, and falls back to it when all objects are lost. On long videos (LVOS V2 valid, pre-specified protocol, three ViT-S seeds), it beats ALGM 0.98 by +2.76 J&F (95% object CI [+1.22,+4.44]; video-cluster [+0.99,+4.52]) at 16% fewer counted encoder FLOPs (0.385 vs. 0.459), sitting 1.0 J&F point below the dense-encoder baseline; at ViT-B the gain over ALGM 0.95 is +3.89 [+2.03,+5.87]. On DAVIS 2017 val it stays within -0.19 J&F of the dense encoder at ViT-S (-0.12 at ViT-B). Controls qualify the result: protecting only the previous mask under ALGM matches or exceeds accuracy at higher FLOPs (0.486), so expectation and surprise mainly reduce counted encoder compute. Practically, lower counted encoder compute did not reduce startup-inclusive mean Cutie step time on a 12-video LVOS sample (3%-8% lower in steady state; an equally engineered ALGM is faster at ViT-S and ViT-B). Section 5.2 separately examines a Cutie permanent-memory schedule and its latency and memory trade-offs. Code: https://github.com/boletoms/focused-cv

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Frozen self-supervised vision transformers such as DINOv3 [ 36 ] give strong dense features, which makes them attractive encoders for video object segmentation (VOS). Their cost grows with the number of patch tokens, and VOS processes every frame at high resolution. Training-free token reduction [ 2 , 27 , 21 , 39 , 22 ] lowers that cost by merging similar tokens, with one rule for the whole image.
blocks.zh: 冷冻自控的视觉变压器如DINOv3[36]给出了强烈的密集特性,这使它们对视频对象分解(VOS)具有吸引力. 其成本随着补丁符数的增加而增加,而VOS以高分辨率处理每个帧. 免训练令牌减少[2, 27, 21, 39, 22] 通过合并类似令牌来降低成本, 对整个图像有一个规则.

blocks.en: VOS offers something these methods do not use: the segmenter’s prediction for the previous frame says where the objects are. A natural design keeps the predicted objects, plus a margin, at full resolution and merges the rest hard. We call the per-patch map that decides how much compute each patch gets a focus map , and its full-resolution patches the focus areas . On short DAVIS clips the closed-loop focus map works: it comes within 1 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} of dense at 0.29 of dense FLOPs, half of what ALGM 0.98 uses (Section 5.6 ). On long videos it fails. Our diagnostics (Section 3.2 ) show why: when a target moves more than two patches between frames, part of it falls outside the margin and is merged with the background; the target is lost, and since the map follows the prediction, it stays lost. On such frames the closed-loop map loses targets nine times as often as dense; away from fast motion it loses them no more often than dense.
blocks.zh: VOS提供了一些这些方法没有使用的东西:分区器对上个帧的预测说出物体的位置. 一个自然设计使所预测的物体,外加一个比值保持了完全的解析度,而将其余的都硬地合并. 我们使用每幅地图来决定每个补丁的计算量, 在短短的DAVIS剪接上,闭路聚焦图工作:它出现在1 J & F\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F}密度为0.29的密度FLOP,是ALGM 0.98使用的一半(第5.6节)。 在长视频上,它失败了。 我们的诊断(第3.2节)显示了为什么:当一个目标在相框之间移动了两个以上的补丁时,它的一部分会落在比值之外并被与背景合并;目标丢失了,由于地图遵循了预测,它仍然丢失了. 在这样的帧上,闭路图丢失目标的次数是密集度的9倍;远离快动,它失去的目标频率不超过密集度.

blocks.en: We propose to stop trusting the last mask: expect where each object will be, then check the frame against that expectation. The method has four parts, all training-free (Figure 1 ): 1. Expectation. For each tracked object, take the union of its velocity-shifted and block-matched masks (found on the current frame’s pooled pixels), grown by one patch (two at ViT-B). This region runs at full resolution. 2. Surprise check. A per-patch mismatch between the current frame and the previous frame shifted by the estimated camera motion, with a variance floor and a small spatial tolerance. Patches that fire are promoted, never demoted. 3. Three tiers. The expectation (high tier) is never merged. Speed-scaled rings, search regions around lost objects and surprise patches (middle tier) are merged by the compared merger’s own rules. Everything else (low tier) is merged by an aggressive budget with a floor of context tokens. 4. Fallback. When every object is lost, the frame runs the compared merger unchanged.

blocks.en: Our contributions are: • A diagnosis of why closed-loop focus maps fail on long videos: fast motion causes compression-induced losses that the loop locks in. • A training-free focus policy that runs at inference time in a trained Cutie head receiving stride-16 features from frozen DINOv3 (tested with one segmenter, Cutie, and one backbone family, DINOv3), conditioning compute on an expectation of object and camera motion, a surprise check, and a fallback to the compared merger. • A pre-specified evaluation: the rule for every adoption decision was written in dated plan files before the run that tested it, and the long-video test pools three heads (one base head fine-tuned with three seeds), at ViT-S and again at ViT-B. We report every run, including failures. • Ablations showing that full resolution in the expected region is necessary, and an exact attribution of where the long-video gain comes from. • A training-free permanent-memory schedule for Cutie (a finding about the segmenter, not the focus map) and, with it, operating points at which the encoder runs at about a third of dense FLOPs at or above dense accuracy on held-out long videos (Section 5.2 ). • A graph-compatible implementation that takes the same decisions as the reference implementation and turns the FLOPs saving into wall-clock speed-ups over dense, with the same engineering applied to the strongest baseline.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: ToMe [ 2 ] merges the most similar token pairs by bipartite matching in every block. ALGM [ 27 ] merges locally in 2 × 2 2\times 2 windows early and globally later with a similarity threshold, designed for segmentation with plain ViTs. AiluRus [ 21 ] adapts resolution to content, PiToMe [ 39 ] preserves the spectrum of the token graph, and Expedite [ 22 ] clusters tokens and reconstructs a dense output. G2TM [ 1 ] coarsens a graph of spatially adjacent tokens and SCMerge [ 32 ] penalises pair merges that break spatial consistency, both for semantic segmentation; DTEM [ 20 ] , unlike the others, learns its merging embeddings. Each applies one rule to the whole image. We port ToMe, ALGM, AiluRus, PiToMe and Expedite from their authors’ code and compare them inside the same VOS model at operating points fixed in advance (Section 4 ). Content-aware token sharing [ 23 ] lets image regions share tokens by content and dynamic token pruning [ 37 ] drops easy tokens in plain-ViT segmenters, both image-level. MPM [ 30 ] pairs mutual nearest neighbours and CubistMerge [ 15 ] keeps the spatial layout so that merging works with window attention and rotary embeddings; both are image-level and use no information from earlier frames.

blocks.en: Segment This Thing [ 34 ] tokenizes finely around a point prompt and coarsely elsewhere, the closest image-level analogue of a focus map, without a previous frame; StructSAM [ 26 ] protects boundary and prompt regions when merging in SAM; PrATo [ 12 ] prunes by a prompt-derived spatial prior; VLTP [ 3 ] prunes by language guidance. In video, for SAM 2 [ 31 ] , Fast SAM2 [ 25 ] prunes encoder outputs by text before propagation; Efficient-SAM2 [ 43 ] keeps full encoder computation in the windows covered by the previous frame’s dilated predicted masks, adds salient windows when tracking confidence is low, and routes the rest through a light branch trained by feature reconstruction; the Recurrent Dynamic Submodel [ 38 ] chooses SAM 2’s blocks per frame with a learned router that reads the previous mask and the current features. Motion-aware ROI prediction [ 13 ] forecasts a target’s crop from its trajectory. Video Patch Pruning [ 14 ] learns to select patches early from the previous frame’s features for video instance segmentation, and MaskVD [ 33 ] masks regions for video detection without training, refreshing full frames periodically. RS 3 -Prune [ 24 ] prunes the readout queries and memory writes of memory-bank VOS without training. Our closed-loop focus map belongs to the family that uses the previous prediction as the prompt. The method we propose differs in where the full-resolution region comes from (an expectation of object and camera motion, corrected on the current frame), in its surprise check, in giving an uncertain middle tier to the compared merger’s own rules, in falling back to that merger when tracking fails, and in its analysis of long videos, where we find that the plain closed-loop map fails.

Video Patch Pruning [14] 学习从前帧的功能中及早选择补丁进行视频实例分解,以及MaskVD[33]口罩区域进行视频检测而不经过训练,定期刷新全帧. blocks.en: Eventful Transformers [ 11 ] and related methods reuse computation for unchanged tokens across frames, and temporal cluster assignment [ 42 ] reuses token clusters. Run-length tokenization [ 7 ] drops patches repeated over time and names camera motion as its failure mode, and vid-TLDR [ 6 ] merges background tokens of video transformers by attention-based saliency. A reuse option we built in the same codebase, in the style of Eventful Transformers (our implementation, not the authors’ code; skipped patches keep their cached output and serve as keys and values), saved at most 2% of FLOPs within one 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} point of the budget alone on DAVIS 2017 val (30 videos, closed-loop maps), and 10 to 15% at a cost of 1.2 to 1.4 points: after the budget, low-interest areas are merged to a floor, and handheld camera motion changes almost every patch. It was not run on long videos or with the expectation focus map. We reduce tokens within each frame; the focus map uses the previous frames only to decide where. Long-video segmenters address memory rather than encoder cost: XMem [ 4 ] and Cutie [ 5 ] keep long-term memories, and SAM2Long [ 10 ] keeps several memory pathways without training. Pollard and Wray [ 28 ] study training-free token merging in video transformers, which merge tokens across space and time with one rule for the whole clip, and report about 2.5 times the speed at a small accuracy cost on action recognition.
blocks.zh: 意外变换器 [11] 和相关方法的再利用计算,用于横跨框架的未变换符,以及时间集群分配 [42]再利用的再利用符号集群. 跑长符号化 [7] 滴出随时间推移而重复的补丁并命名相机运动作为其故障模式,而vid-TLDR [6] 将视频变速器的背景符号通过以注意力为主的显著性来合并. 我们在同一代码库中构建的再利用选项, 风格是意外变形器(我们的执行, 不是作者的代码; 跳过补丁保留其缓存输出并充当键和值), 它没有在长视频上运行,也没有在预期焦点地图上运行。 我们在每个框内减少符;焦点图只用上个框来决定位置. 长视频分机地址为内存而非编码器成本:XMem [4]和Cutie [5] 保持长期记忆,而SAM2Long [10] 保持了多条没有经过训练的内存路径. Pollard和Wray [28] 研究在视频变压器中进行无培训的活字符号合并,将全时空活字符号与整段剪辑的一条规则相融合,并以小精度成本报告速度的2.5倍左右的动作识别.

blocks.en: Cutie [ 5 ] reads object-level memory to segment each frame; LVOS [ 17 ] measures long-term VOS, where losses and re-appearances dominate. We keep Cutie unchanged except its pixel encoder, whose stride-16 features come from the frozen ViT under each method; its memory readout and decoder are identical for every method and excluded from the compute we report. For SAM 2, SAM2Dual [ 19 ] adds a training-free long-term memory filled by interval sampling to a short-term one, a memory schedule in the spirit of Appendix D but for a different segmenter and without an encoder-compute saving; and the codec-guided compressor of Sheng et al. [ 35 ] , for video language models, uses compressed-video motion vectors as a prior for merging tokens across frames, which is temporal and training-free but not tied to a segmenter’s predicted objects. SAMURAI [ 41 ] adds a training-free Kalman motion model to SAM 2’s memory selection for tracking, and EdgeTAM [ 44 ] and EfficientTAM [ 40 ] replace SAM 2’s image encoder by lighter trained ones and also make its memory attention cheaper; none of them changes the encoder’s compute per frame from the segmenter’s predictions.
blocks.zh: Cutie [5] 读取对象级内存来分出每个帧; LVOS [17] 度量长期VOS,其中损失和再出占主导. 我们让Cutie保持不变,除了它的像素编码器,它的strip-16特性来自每种方法下的被冻结的VIT;它的内存读出和解码器对每一种方法都是一样的,并且被排除在我们报告的计算之外. 对于SAM 2, SAM2Dual [19] 将一个以间隔采样方式填充的无训练长期内存添加到一个短期内存中,这是按照附录D的精神,但对于一个不同的分节器,且没有编码器计算保存的内存时间表;而Sheng等的编码制导压缩器 [35] 对于视频语言模型,使用压缩-视频活性向量作为跨帧合并活性符号的先行方式,这是时间性的,没有训练,但并没有绑在分节器预测对象上. SAMURAI [41] 在SAM 2的内存选择中添加了无训练的卡尔曼运动模型来进行跟踪,而EdgeTAM [44]和EffectTAM [40] 将SAM 2的图像编码器取而代之,取而代之的是经过更轻训练的编码器,也使其内存注意力更便宜;它们都没有改变编码器从分机的预测中每帧的计算.

blocks.en: 3.1 Setting
blocks.zh: 3.1 设置

blocks.en: The encoder is a frozen DINOv3 ViT (ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/16 as checks) with 4 register tokens and RoPE positions. A method may merge patch tokens between attention and MLP in any block. Each token carries its size (how many original patches it holds), a size-weighted position used for RoPE, and its tier. After the last block every original patch takes the output of the token that holds it (unmerge), so Cutie’s decoder receives a full stride-16 feature map. The ViT is never trained; Cutie’s remaining modules are trained once per head with the ViT dense (Section 4 ).

blocks.en: 3.2 Why a closed-loop focus map fails on long videos
blocks.zh: 3.2 国家 关闭- loop 焦点映射为何在长视频上失败

blocks.en: The closed-loop focus map protects every patch the previous prediction touches, grown by one patch (two at ViT-B), and merges the rest with a budget: in every block bipartite matching merges the remaining low-tier tokens among themselves at a nominal rate of 0.7, which pairing caps at one half, and never below 64 of them remain. It comes within 1 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} of dense on DAVIS at 0.29 of dense FLOPs (Table 5 ) but falls below ALGM on long videos (paired differences from − 5.38 -5.38 to − 0.10 -0.10 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} across the heads we tested on LVOS V1 val).
blocks.zh: 闭合-loop焦点图保护了前作预测所触碰的每一个补丁,由一补丁(在Vit-B上为两个)所生长,其余部分与预算相合并:在每一个区块双相匹配时,各自将剩余的低等活符以0.7的标定速率进行合并,两者相配的上限为一分之一,永远不能低于64. 它位于1 J & F\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F}在高密度FLOPs上密度为0.29(表5),但在长相视频上低于ALGM(在LVOS V1 val上测试的头部的J & F\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F}之间出现差异)。

blocks.en: Logged runs on the development split (LVOS V2 train) locate the cause. The share of a tracked target outside the protected patches grows with its displacement since the previous frame: 0.6% under one patch, 12.1% at 2 to 4 patches, 31.5% beyond 4 patches. LVOS runs at 6 frames per second, so this lag is geometric and the same for every map source, including the previous ground truth. On frames where a target moves more than two patches (about 8% of tracked frames), the closed-loop map loses it on 2.81% of frames, against 0.30% for dense and 0.36% for ALGM (each rate counts the frames on which that method was still tracking the target, so the three come from different sets of frames); on all other frames the three are equal (0.01 to 0.03%). Ninety-six percent of its loss onsets fall on fast frames. Losses are not always permanent (92% of the closed-loop map’s visible-loss onsets recovered, 741 of 809, on the development split), but the deficit against ALGM sits in the frames where the closed-loop map is lost and ALGM tracks. The losses are compression-induced (the lagging part of the target is merged with background), and the loop locks them in. Remedies tried on the closed-loop map, a dense I-frame every 5 frames and dense I-frames triggered by evidence of the target outside the map, helped on development videos but not on LVOS V1 val; this led to the design below, which replaces full resets by an expectation, a surprise check and the fallback.

blocks.en: 3.3 Expectation (high tier)
blocks.zh: 3.3 期望值(高水平)

blocks.en: For each object we maintain a run-time state: its last mask, centroid, and velocity estimated from predictions at t − 1 t{-}1 and t − 2 t{-}2 , together with a separate history of up to 10 tracked-mask areas. In the runtime controller, an object counts as lost when its predicted mask area falls below a tenth of the median of those last 10 tracked areas, or below 16 pixels (distinct from the ground-truth IoU < 0.1 <0.1 loss definition used in the outcome analysis of Section 5.3 ). For each tracked object, we take the union of the velocity-shifted and block-matched masks—(a) its last mask shifted by its centroid velocity and (b) its last mask shifted by the displacement that best matches its template between the previous and the current frame on 4 × 4 4\times 4 -pooled pixels (search within 8 patches)—and grow that union by one patch (two at ViT-B). Object masks are taken at patch level (a patch belongs to the mask at 1% coverage; the template uses the patches covered at least half, or the mask if there are none). The high tier is the union over objects, plus the previous prediction and its velocity shift; before the expected regions are added, the base map from the previous prediction is rounded up to the next multiple of 64 patches with its nearest unprotected patches (at most 63 extra, as for the closed-loop map). The high tier is never merged, although its tokens still attend to merged ones. Offline on 420 development videos, this expectation covers 93.3% of fast-moving targets against 77.8% for the one-patch margin, with 31% more area on those frames (10% over all frames); it was chosen by a rule fixed before that measurement.

blocks.en: 3.4 Surprise check
blocks.zh: 3.4 突击检查

blocks.en: A surprise is any deviation from the expected frame. For each patch p p outside the expectation we compare the current frame’s pooled pixels at p p with the previous frame’s at p − g p-g , where g g is the integer camera shift (within 4 patches) that best aligns the two frames. The mismatch is normalised per patch with a variance floor σ = 0.05 \sigma=0.05 and takes the best of nine offsets of up to 4 pixels; a patch fires at e ≥ 0.06 e\geq 0.06 , the highest threshold that reached 95% recall on both offline event sets (targets entering outside the map, and re-appearances). Content entering at the image border always fires. A fired patch inside an object’s ring or search region joins the high tier; any other fired patch joins the middle tier. If more than half of the patches outside the base map fire (a frame-wide change such as a cut or fast camera motion), all of them join the middle tier while the expectation stays whole. Surprise only promotes: false positives cost compute, false negatives cost accuracy, and we prefer the former.

blocks.en: 3.6 Fallback

blocks.en: When every object that has appeared is lost, or the map is empty, the frame runs the compared merger exactly (plain ALGM 0.98 at ViT-S); the expectation observes passively so its state stays current. On the held-out protocol the fallback runs on 29.6% of frames (three heads); Section 5.3 shows the gain is not produced by these frames.

blocks.en: 3.7 Compute accounting

blocks.en: We count whole-encoder FLOPs per frame from what the forward pass did: projections on the tokens entering attention, attention per computed query–key pair, MLP on the tokens left after merging, the patch embedding, and every operation a method adds (matching, clustering, and our feature products for the camera search, block matching and the surprise mismatch). Norms, softmax and RoPE are omitted for every method alike. We report the ratio to dense, averaged per frame (frame-weighted across videos); dense frames inside a method’s run count 1.0. Cutie’s memory and decoder are identical across methods and excluded. The count follows the tokens a method keeps; the timed implementation’s padded buffers and redone blocks are overhead of that implementation and appear only in wall clock. Wall clock is measured separately (Section 5.8 ).
blocks.zh: 我们从前方的通行证中计算出每个帧的全编码器FLOP:对进入注意的符号的预测、对计算出来的查询对一对的注意、对合并后留下的符号的MLP、补丁嵌入,以及每个操作都添加了一种方法(匹配、集群和我们用于相机搜索的特性产品、块匹配和出乎意料的不匹配)。 对于每一种方法,都省略了规范、软马克和ROPE。 我们报告密度与每帧平均值的比例(帧加权于视频之间), Cutie的记忆和解码器在方法上是相同的,被排除在外。 计数遵循一种方法所保存的符号;定时执行的加分缓冲和重排区块是执行的间接费用,只出现在墙上钟上。 墙钟单独测量(第5.8节)。

blocks.en: 3.8 Timed implementation
blocks.zh: 3.8 及时执行

blocks.en: A direct implementation is bound by the host: per-frame Python work, host reads of token counts and many small kernels outweigh the work it removes. With the method unchanged, the timed implementation keeps every step before the encoder on the GPU (two host reads per frame), sizes each block’s token buffer from the previous frame’s counts (a frame that exceeds a buffer is redone from that block on, so outputs never depend on the guess), captures every step in CUDA graphs, compiles each block segment, uses variable-length flash attention [ 8 ] , and overlaps block 0’s attention with the tier planning. It equals its own eager form bit for bit, rounds every bf16 intermediate as the reference path does, and takes the reference path’s decisions: replaying the ground-truth masks of all 140 long videos through both, the fallback decision agrees on every frame and the tiers on all but one of 61,880 frames (an fp32 centroid at exactly half a pixel; Appendix A ). Every number of the method in Tables 1 – 7 comes from this implementation unless marked; baselines run their ported code.
blocks.zh: 直接执行受主机约束:每帧Python活字,主机读取符数和许多小内核都超过它去掉的工作. 由于方法不变,定时执行保留了GPU上编码器之前的每一个步骤(每个帧有两个主机读取),每个块的符号缓冲从上个帧的计数(一个超过缓冲的帧是从该块上重接而来,所以输出从不依赖于猜取),捕获了CUDA图表中的每个步骤,编译了每个块段,使用可变长的闪光注意[8],并且将0块的注意力与分级规划相重叠. 它等于它自己的急切形式位点,像参考路径一样环绕每个bf16中间体,并采纳参考路径的决定:通过两种方式重新播放所有140个长相视频的地真口罩,倒置决定同意除了61,880个帧(一个Fp32个半像素的中间体;附录A ) 以外的所有帧和分级。 表1至表7中每一方法的编号均来自这一执行,除非标明;基线使用其端口编码。

blocks.en: Cutie (small) with its pixel encoder’s stride-16 features replaced by the frozen DINOv3 ViT under each method; the stride-8 and stride-4 skips come from Cutie’s own ResNet-18 stem. Heads (Cutie’s modules other than the ViT) are trained with the ViT frozen and dense on DAVIS 2017 train and MOSE train [ 9 ] with Cutie’s training script; we do not train on YouTube-VOS or static images ourselves. Each head starts from the official Cutie small weights ( cutie-small-mega ; all non-ViT tensors except the two new stride-16 projections), which their authors trained with static-image pre-training and on DAVIS, YouTube-VOS, MOSE, BURST and OVIS, so our heads inherit that training; trains the projections for 5,000 iterations and then everything for 40,000 (batch 2). The long-video heads are fine-tuned from one such base head for 10,000 iterations with three Cutie seeds, so they share the base head’s 45,000 iterations: R31c, h2 and h3 at ViT-S, and R41 b1 to b3 (from head R25) at ViT-B. blocks.en: 5.4 Do the safety nets cover the objects?
blocks.zh: 5.4 (中文(简体) ). 安全网覆盖物体吗?

blocks.en: The premise is that the segmenter’s previous mask misses fast objects and the expectation, the ring, the search region and the surprise check repair this. We measured it frame by frame (development split, 34 videos, one head, 36,450 object-frames; per frame the share of an object’s ground-truth pixels inside each region). Table 4 gives the share inside the previous mask moved by the expected motion, inside the high tier the encoder finally ran, and inside the high or middle tier. For objects that move more than two patches per frame (17% of object-frames) the moved mask misses a third of the frames (below 0.9 coverage on 33%); the final high tier misses 2%, and high or middle 19 of the 6,050 fast object-frames (0.31%). Slow objects need no repair (1% misses). The nets therefore do what they were built for. They do not make the segmenter find a lost target: in the first five frames after an object reappears (302 object-frames) the object lies 97% inside the protected tiers, and on frames where it is visible but the prediction is empty (428 object-frames) 94% inside them, yet the object’s J (IoU) is 0.51 and 0 there (a descriptive count over the same frames, not a causal test). What limits long videos at that point is the segmenter’s matching, not the encoder’s coverage; Appendix D shows a memory policy that acts on exactly this.

blocks.en: The timed implementation turns the FLOPs saving into a speed-up over dense on all three backbones (Table 7 ). ALGM given the same engineering is faster at ViT-S and ViT-B although it does more FLOPs (0.49 and 0.51 against 0.36 and 0.44 on these clips; 0.57 against 0.40 at ViT-L): our budget merges in every block and the expectation step take time that FLOPs do not count. A kernel profile of 60 frames places the difference in that bookkeeping: per frame the method launches about 820 (ViT-S) and 860 (ViT-B) GPU kernels against ALGM’s 470, and its extra GPU time at ViT-S is in precision casts, gathers and scatters and small element-wise kernels (0.61 ms), not in attention or matrix products (0.07 ms). At ViT-L, where the encoder dominates, the method is as fast as ALGM (9.25 against 9.46 ms). With deterministic kernels the ViT-S speed-up over dense is small (1.05 × \times ) and ALGM is faster than the method at every size. These clips start from ground-truth masks, so no frame falls back. Inside real long-video evaluations the gain shrinks. On 12 LVOS videos (6,516 frames, Cutie’s own predicted masks, so the fallback runs on 39% of frames at ViT-S and 49% at ViT-B; an idle GPU) the encoder takes a median 4.20 ms against dense Cutie’s 5.35 ms at ViT-S and 5.32 against 8.03 ms at ViT-B (means after each video’s first 30 frames: 4.58 against 5.32 and 6.17 against 7.96), but the encoder is only 34% to 44% of Cutie’s step, so the whole step falls by 3% at ViT-S (15.18 against 15.63 ms) and 8% at ViT-B (16.81 against 18.33 ms) in that steady state. The first frames of each video (graph capture and buffer sizing) cost about 1.4 s at ViT-S, so over videos of this length (543 frames on average) the mean step is 13% above dense at ViT-S (17.65 against 15.57 ms) and 6% above at ViT-B (19.30 against 18.27 ms), the medians are 5% and 11% below, and the 99th percentile of the encoder is about four times dense’s (24.8 against 6.2 ms at ViT-S). On this 12-video sample, mean Cutie step time including startup was higher than for dense Cutie; the speed-up over dense holds for the encoder, in steady state, and grows with video length as the startup cost is spread. A rerun of the whole table after the fixes of Appendix B agrees with it within 1% (4% for deterministic ALGM at ViT-L). The threshold-0.5 setting of Section 5.5 (an ablation that was not adopted, because its held-out lower bound missed the rule; 0.313 against 0.388 FLOPs in the ViT-S reference run with default memory) was timed in closed loop on the same 12 videos (not the scheduled variant of Section 5.2 , which was not timed) and times a little lower: the encoder takes a median 3.94 ms at ViT-S and 5.09 ms at ViT-B (means after each video’s first 30 frames 4.22 and 5.78 ms), and the whole step after startup 14.78 ms (5% below dense) and 16.39 ms (11% below). The 19% reduction in counted encoder FLOPs from the ViT-S reference experiment thus corresponds to about 2 to 3 percentage points of steady-state step time in this separate timing measurement, because the encoder is a minority of the step. On the frames where the focus map itself runs (the non-fallback frames) the method’s whole step after startup is 16.10 ms at ViT-S against dense Cutie’s 15.63 ms and 18.37 against 18.33 ms at ViT-B, which is consistent with the steady-state saving of the main setting coming from the 39% and 49% of frames on which the fallback (plain ALGM) runs (the comparison is unmatched: dense Cutie’s mean is over all frames and per-frame records were not kept); with the threshold-0.5 setting the non-fallback frames take 15.64 and 16.90 ms. Plain ALGM was also run in this closed-loop harness (Cutie’s own masks, 12 videos), but only on the eager path: encoder median 7.70 ms against dense Cutie’s 5.35 ms at ViT-S, and 7.68 against 8.03 ms at ViT-B. This is a different condition from Table 7 , the equally engineered encoder benchmark with ground-truth histories, where ALGM is faster than the method at ViT-S and ViT-B; we did not engineer ALGM in closed loop, so the two conditions must not be mixed and the comparison with an equally engineered ALGM rests on Table 7 .
blocks.zh: 定时实施将节省的FLOP转化为所有三个主干线上密集度的加速(表7)。 ALGM在ViT-S和ViT-B的同一工程速度更快,尽管它做更多的FLOP(0.49和0.51对0.36和0.44对这些片段;0.57对0.40对ViT-L):我们的预算在每个区块合并,预期步骤需要时间,FLOP不计算。 60帧的内核剖面将这种记账方式的区别放在了:每帧的方法发射出约820个(ViT-S)和860个(ViT-B)GPU内核对ALGM的470,而它在ViT-S的外加GPU时间是精确的铸出,收发和散发以及小元素的内核(0.61 ms),不在注意或矩阵产品中(0.07 ms). 在以编码器为主的ViT-L,方法快于ALGM(9.25对9.46ms). 有定心内核的ViT-S超密集速度小于(1.05×\times),ALGM快于每个大小的方法. 这些片段是从地上真口罩开始的,所以没有框倒后. 在真实的长视频评价中,收益会收缩. 在12个LVOS视频(6,516帧,Cutie自己的预测口罩,因此倒置在了ViT-S的39%和ViT-B的49%;闲置的GPU)上,编码器在ViT-S的5.35m和ViT-B的5.32之间取中值4.20ms,在ViT-S的8.03m之间取中值(指每段视频的前30m之后:4.58对5.32和6.17对7.96),但编码器在Cutie的步数上只有34%到44%,因此整个步数在ViT-S(15.18对15.63ms)和ViT-B(16.81对18.33ms)在稳定状态下降了3%。 每个视频(图捕捉和缓冲分解)的第一帧在Vit-S大约花费了1.4 s,因此在这个长度的视频(平均543 帧)上,Vit-S(17.65对15.57 ms)的中位数比密度高13%,而Vit-B(19.30对18.27 ms)的中位数比密度高6%,编码器的中位数为5%和11%,编码器中位数大约是密度的4倍(24.8对6.2 ms对Vit-S). 在这个12个视频样本中,包括启动在内的Cutie步骤时间比稠密的Cutie要高;编码器速度超过密集的状态,处于平稳状态,随着启动成本的分散而随视频长度而增长. 在附录B的修复后,整个表格的重排在1%之内(确定ALGM在Vit-L的4%)。 第5.5节的阈值-0.5设定(没有采用这一设定,因为其被搁置的下限错过了规则;在带有默认内存的Vit-S参考运行中,0.313和0.388的FLOP)在同一12个视频(不是第5.2节的预定变体,没有定时)上被用闭环来定时,而且次数略低:编码器在Vit-S为中位数3.94毫秒,在Vit-B为中位数5.09毫秒(指每段视频的前30帧4.22和5.78毫秒后),在启动14.78毫秒(密度以下5%)和16.39毫秒(以下11%)后整个步骤。 因此,从Vit-S参考实验中计算出的编码器FLOP减少19%,这相当于这一单独计时测量中稳定状态步骤时间的2至3个百分点左右,因为编码器是该步骤的少数. 在焦点图本身运行的相框(非倒回相框)上,方法启动后的整个步骤在Vit-S对稠密的Cutie的15.63分和18.37分和在Vit-B对18.33分的相框上是16.10分;这符合从39%和49%的相框(Permanal ALGM)所运行的相框(比较无比:稠密的Cutie的平均值已超过所有相框,而且没有保留每帧记录);设定非倒回相框的阈值为15.64分和16.90分。 Plain ALGM也运行在这种闭锁-放管(Cutie自己的口罩,12个视频)中,但只在急切的道路上:编码器中位数为7.70 ms,而密密的Cutie在Vit-S的5.35 ms,在Vit-B的7.68 ms。 这与表7不同,表7是具有地面真实历史的同样设计编码器基准,在表7中,ALGM比Vit-S和Vit-B中的方法更快;我们没有在闭环循环中设计ALGM,因此这两个条件决不能混合,与同样设计的ALGM的比较取决于表7。

blocks.en: 5.9 A second baseline: ToMe
blocks.zh: 5.9 (中文(简体) ). 第二个基线:托梅

blocks.en: We applied the same design with ToMe as the compared merger (ToMe’s matching on the middle tier, plain ToMe r64 as the fallback). The first version is − 2.26 -2.26 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} [ − 3.93 , − 0.71 ] [-3.93,\,-0.71] against plain ToMe r64 at 0.449 against 0.709 FLOPs on the held-out protocol, so it is not non-inferior: ToMe merges a fixed 64 tokens per block, and once the budget has thinned the low tier those merges fall on the middle tier. A second version (ToMe’s rule as a rate on the tiers) failed its development gate and was not validated. A third version adds two rules aimed at the failure modes found on development videos: a frame whose tracked object moves at the block-matching radius runs plain ToMe, and frames Cutie writes to memory run plain ToMe. It passed its gate and on the held-out protocol is non-inferior at 21% lower FLOPs ( − 0.68 -0.68 [ − 1.56 , + 0.10 ] [-1.56,\,+0.10] at 0.557 against 0.709), not superior. Both numbers are from a rerun after a fix: the fallback frames of the first run let the focus map’s interest leak into ToMe’s merging (Appendix B ), and the first-run values were − 2.23 -2.23 and − 0.45 -0.45 . The held-out videos judged the ToMe arm twice, and both revisions were designed on the development split after the first failure; we report every attempt. With ToMe the design saves compute at ToMe’s accuracy; with ALGM it also gains accuracy.
blocks.zh: 我们应用了与ToMe相同的设计来进行比较合并(ToMe在中层的比对上,Plain ToMe r64作为倒数倒数). 第一个版本是- 2.26 - 2.26 J & F\mathcal{ J}\&\mathcal{F} [- 3.93,- 0.71] [-3.93,\,-0.71] 对被搁置协议上的平原ToMe r64 at 0.449对 0.709 FLOPs, 所以它不是非地狱: ToMe将每块固定的64个令牌合并起来,一旦预算缩小了低层,这些合并就会落在中层。 第二个版本(ToMe规则作为分级率)未能通过开发门,没有被验证. 第三个版本增加了两个针对开发视频中发现的失败模式的规则:一个被跟踪对象在块相匹配半径上移动的帧运行为平坦的ToMe,而帧 Cutie写为内存运行为平坦的ToMe. 它经过了大门,在停放协议上,低于21%的FLOP(− 0.68-0.68 [− 1.56, + 0.10] [-1.56,\,+0.10] 在0.557对0.709)为非地狱,不优越。 两个数字都是从固定后重跑而来:第一回跑的倒计时框让焦点地图的兴趣渗出到ToMe的合并(Appendix B)中去,而第一回跑的数值是−2.23 -2.23和−0.45 -0.45. 被搁置的影片对ToMe手臂进行了两次判断,两次修改都是针对第一次失败后的开发分裂设计的;我们报告每次尝试. 使用 ToMe 设计可以节省 ToMe 的准确性; 使用 ALGM , 也能提高准确性 。

blocks.zh: 6 限制

blocks.en: • Second baseline. Against ToMe the design is non-inferior at lower FLOPs, not superior, and only after two revisions made after a held-out failure. • Wall clock. The encoder is faster than dense in steady state, but Cutie’s whole step falls by only 3% to 8% in closed loop on LVOS and, with per-video startup, is not faster than dense on videos of about 540 frames (Section 5.8 ); at ViT-S and ViT-B the encoder is slower than ALGM’s given the same engineering; with deterministic kernels the ViT-S speed-up over dense is small and ALGM is faster at every size. The ViT-L timed path has an unresolved intermittent crash, with the overlap on and off, that required relaunching long runs (Appendix B ); the ViT-L timing (114 frames) completed with the overlap on. • Fallback share. blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: A frozen DINOv3 ViT inside a trained Cutie head can spend its compute where the segmenter expects the objects to be. Under the pre-specified long-video protocol (LVOS V2 valid, three heads at ViT-S and ViT-B), full resolution in the expected region, the compared merger’s own rules in an uncertain middle tier, and fallback when tracking fails beat ALGM at lower counted encoder FLOPs ( + 2.76 +2.76 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} at 16% fewer FLOPs at ViT-S; + 3.89 +3.89 at ViT-B) and stay within 0.2 0.2 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} of the dense encoder on DAVIS 2017 val. The prior-mask ALGM control shows how much accuracy full resolution on the previous prediction already achieves at higher compute ( 0.486 0.486 FLOPs), while the expectation and surprise tiers operate below ALGM’s FLOPs with a small accuracy trade-off. Separately, a training-free permanent-memory schedule for Cutie lifts every encoder on long videos (reaching 73.61 73.61 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} at 0.335 0.335 encoder FLOPs with τ = 0.5 \tau=0.5 , level with scheduled dense), at a + 49 % +49\% median step-time and 6 × 6\times GPU-memory cost (Section 5.2 , Appendix D ). Finally, counted encoder FLOPs do not translate into wall-clock savings on our 12-video LVOS sample (mean startup-inclusive step time is above dense Cutie, and an equally engineered ALGM is faster at ViT-S and ViT-B; Section 5.8 ). Speed beyond an equally engineered ALGM at small backbones, and superiority over a second baseline, remain open.

blocks.en: Three implementation differences were found and fixed before the reported rows, each by checking that the timed implementation took the reference path’s decisions: compiled kernels kept fp32 intermediates where the reference path rounds to bf16 (fixed by emulating the casts); ALGM’s threshold statistics were built in fp32 where the reference path keeps them in bf16 (fixed); and a lost object’s search region grew to the whole frame after a loss longer than the frame’s width plus height in patches, which only long videos contain (fixed). A replay of the ground-truth masks of all 140 long videos through both implementations, at the ViT-S and ViT-B settings, agrees on every fallback decision and on the tiers of all but one of 61,880 frames. On fallback frames the timed implementation does not compute the expectation’s products, which no later frame reads, and its counted FLOPs exclude them.

ViT-L runs. The method’s ViT-L timed path crashes intermittently, with an illegal memory access in an encoder graph replay a few seconds into a new video, with and without MPS and with the side-stream overlap (block 0’s attention beside the planning step) on and off. On a fixed 13-video sequence the crash reproduces at the 13th video and disappears with the overlap off or when the tracker’s stale per-state graphs are never destroyed, but on the full run neither change prevents it (a run with the overlap off crashed after 10 videos, and so did one that kept the stale graphs). It persists with synchronous kernel launches, with the side graph replayed on the main stream, with separate graph pools, with the allocator’s expandable segments off and with the device synchronized before each destroy, so it is not a stream race. The cause is open. The reported ViT-L rows come from one mode: overlap off, one process, no MPS, relaunched after each crash (rows are written per video, and the video a crash interrupted reruns from its start): three crashes in the first 42 videos, none in the remaining 98 videos and the 30 short clips. The overlap only reorders work; a rerun of three videos saved with the overlap on gave identical rows for two and object differences of + 0.6 +0.6 and + 1.7 +1.7 J for the third, within the timed implementation’s rerun variation. ViT-S and ViT-B rows and timings ran with the overlap and never crashed.

blocks.en: Appendix D A permanent-memory schedule for Cutie
blocks.zh: 附录D 可爱的永久纪念时间表

blocks.en: This appendix reports a finding about Cutie’s memory, not about the focus map, and the controls that show it. Cutie writes a working-memory frame every fifth frame and evicts old ones; masks given by the user are permanent. On long videos the object is lost for want of old, clean anchors. The schedule writes every 20th frame, with Cutie’s own predicted mask, to the permanent memory (the method also runs that frame at full resolution, as an I-frame; dense Cutie runs every frame at full resolution anyway). Periodic and permanent memories are not new in themselves: XMem [ 4 ] and Cutie keep the given annotation permanently, and SAM2Dual [ 19 ] fills a long-term memory by interval sampling; what we report is the effect of a 20-frame permanent write of Cutie’s own predictions, with controls on three encoders. No training; each object receives its standard first-appearance annotation, and scheduled writes store the model’s own predictions. It was chosen on the development split (420 LVOS V2 train videos, one head) from seven frame schedules (a dense or fallback frame every 10, 20 or 30 frames, or on loss; none passed its pre-specified gate alone) and three memory treatments (forced write, clearing then writing, permanent write; only the permanent write passed), and then run once on the held-out videos with all three heads. Because the held-out gain was far larger than the development gain and above dense, controls were added: plain ALGM 0.98 and dense Cutie with the same schedule on the same videos.

Cutie每第五帧写出一个工作记忆相框并驱逐出旧相框;用户提供的口罩是永久相框. 在长视频中,对象丢失是因为缺少旧的,干净的锚. 计时表每20个帧都会写出Cutie自己预想的口罩给永久内存(这种方法也以完全分辨率运行这个帧,作为I-帧;密集的Cutie以完全分辨率运行每个帧). 定期和永久的记忆本身并不新鲜:XMem [4]和Cutie永久保留给定的注释,而SAM2Dual [19]通过间隔取样填补了长期记忆;我们报告的是Cutie自己预测的20帧永久写出的效果,对3个编码器有控制. 没有训练;每个对象都会收到其标准的首次出现说明,预定的写作会存储模型自己的预测. 它在开发分拆(420 LVOS V2 列车视频,1个头)时从7个帧表(每10个,20个或30个帧,或损失一个密集或倒置的帧;没有一个单通过它预先指定的门)和3个内存处理(强制写出,清理后写出,永久写出;只有永久写出后通过)中被选中,然后在被搁置的视频上运行一次,所有3个头. 由于被搁置的增益远大于开发增益并超过密集度,因此增加了控制:平原ALGM 0.98和密集的Cutie在同一视频上拥有相同的时间表.

At equal schedule our method is + 3.34 +3.34 [ + 1.91 , + 4.94 ] [+1.91,\,+4.94] over ALGM 0.98 at 0.413 against 0.486 FLOPs ( + 1.42 +1.42 [ − 0.95 , + 4.21 ] [-0.95,\,+4.21] on the 600-frame-plus videos, + 3.23 +3.23 [ + 1.48 , + 5.13 ] [+1.48,\,+5.13] on the 90 new videos), and − 0.06 -0.06 [ − 1.03 , + 0.92 ] [-1.03,\,+0.92] against dense with the schedule ( + 1.48 +1.48 [ − 1.65 , + 4.37 ] [-1.65,\,+4.37] and − 0.75 -0.75 [ − 1.75 , + 0.23 ] [-1.75,\,+0.23] ). The paper’s claim therefore holds under both memory regimes. On the 316 development videos not used to choose the schedule (one head, R26; all at most 600 frames, since the 44 longer ones were in the selection set) the gains are smaller and in the same direction: dense Cutie + 0.71 +0.71 [ + 0.11 , + 1.36 ] [+0.11,\,+1.36] , ours + 1.13 +1.13 [ + 0.40 , + 1.89 ] [+0.40,\,+1.89] , ALGM 0.98 + 1.33 +1.33 [ + 0.53 , + 2.29 ] [+0.53,\,+2.29] (454 objects); at equal schedule ours is + 0.96 +0.96 [ + 0.31 , + 1.73 ] [+0.31,\,+1.73] over ALGM and − 0.85 -0.85 [ − 1.66 , − 0.16 ] [-1.66,\,-0.16] against dense with the schedule, so on shorter videos dense with the schedule is ahead of ours. The effect grows with video length, and the 600-frame-plus videos are covered only by the held-out run. We keep the schedule out of the method (Section 5.2 reports it as an operating point): it is a property of the segmenter, it was selected with the held-out videos of the method still unused for it only in part (they had served the method before), and it needs fresh data and an end-to-end cost before adoption. The encoder FLOPs do not count Cutie’s own cost, and it is not small: the permanent memory grows by one frame per 20 frames, and over 12 long videos (6,516 frames, dense encoder, ViT-S, an otherwise idle GPU, one process per setting) the median time of Cutie’s whole step per frame rises from 14.3 to 21.3 ms ( + 49 +49 %; mean 15.2 to 26.2 ms, + 73 +73 %; 90th percentile 17.5 to 47.9 ms, 99th 31.0 to 62.1 ms) while the encoder stays at 5.0 ms (an earlier run of the same videos gave a median 14.9 to 21.8 ms, + 47 +47 %). The schedule’s cost therefore exceeds the encoder time that any token reduction can save (5.0 ms of a 14.3 ms step), and it grows with the length of the video. Peak GPU memory of dense Cutie for the whole process rises from 1.08 GiB without the schedule to 6.45 GiB with it (peak allocated; reserved 1.25 to 6.82 GiB); the schedule’s permanent memory is a real cost, not a rounding.
